title: Beyond the 956: E-bike battery explosion destroys Oregon family home; six escape, cat dies
excerpt: A lithium-ion e-bike battery exploded inside a Troutdale, Oregon, home on Thursday night, November 5, setting the house ablaze within minutes. All six people inside escaped without injury, but the family's cat died and the home was destroyed.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A lithium-ion battery removed from an electric bike exploded inside a family home in Troutdale, Oregon, on Thursday night, November 5, 2026, and the house was engulfed in flames within minutes, according to fire officials and local news reports. All six people inside escaped without injury, but the family's cat died and the five-bedroom, two-story home was destroyed.

Home security video captured the battery bursting into flames in the living room of the home on East Historic Columbia River Highway, near Portland. The battery had been taken off the e-bike and was resting on a padded chair when it began smoking and then exploded, the homeowner told local television stations. Gresham Fire crews responded to heavy flames coming from the wood-frame house, and investigators determined the fire was caused by the lithium-ion e-bike battery, the fire department said.

Accounts differ on whether the battery was plugged in at the time. Gresham Fire Battalion Chief Shawn Durham told KATU that investigators determined the battery exploded while it was charging, while the homeowner and witnesses told KPTV and KGW that it was unplugged and sitting on the chair when it began smoking and popping.

The homeowner, Kari Ann Peniche, said the fire spread within seconds, leaving the family almost no time to get out. She alerted the couple renting the upstairs unit, and all six residents made it out safely. The family lost nearly everything they owned, Peniche said.

The fire is the latest in a growing number of lithium-ion battery fires in Oregon. The Oregon State Fire Marshal counted 649 such incidents statewide from 2020 through 2025, with the yearly total rising from 74 in 2020 to 161 in 2025. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has warned against using incompatible universal chargers with e-bikes, saying they can increase the risk of battery fires.

Sources: CBS News TikTok, Nov. 11, 2026; BBC News; KGW; KATU; KPTV; KOIN; Firehouse; New York Post, Nov. 10-11, 2026.
